profile.name: Floss
profile.tagline: A rhythmic dance move characterized by rapid, alternating arm and hip swings.
profile.insight: While popularized by Russell Horning in 2017, the earliest documented instance of the dance dates back to an October 2010 video on the YouTube channel Ryan Mayall.
profile.profile: The Floss is a dance and internet meme involving the rapid, alternating swinging of clenched fists from behind the body to the front. It gained global prominence through social media, television appearances, and its inclusion as an emote in the video game Fortnite Battle Royale.
profile.profile_long:
The Floss, also known as the 'dental floss dance' or 'baile del hilo dental', is a movement-based dance characterized by the rapid, repetitive swinging of arms with clenched fists. The motion involves moving the arms from the back of the body to the front on alternating sides, accompanied by counter-hip movements. The name is derived from the visual impression of the movements, which resemble the act of using a large, invisible piece of dental floss. 

The dance's history is rooted in early internet video culture. While it achieved viral status in 2017, the earliest documented instance of the dance was published on October 18, 2010, by the YouTube channel Ryan Mayall. Another early instance was promoted in a 2014 clip by JStuStudios, featuring content creators Justin Stewart and Andrew Scites, who referred to the move as 'The Squeege'. The dance reached a massive global audience in May 2017, when 14-year-old Russell Horning, known as 'the backpack kid', performed the move during a live Saturday Night Live performance of Katy Perry's song 'Swish Swish'. 

Following this performance, the Floss became a widespread trend among children and teenagers, appearing on numerous children's television channels and in mainstream media such as The Simpsons. Its popularity was further cemented by its inclusion as a limited-time emote in the 2017 video game Fortnite Battle Royale. This integration led to the dance becoming a common sight in schools, though it also sparked controversy. In December 2018, Horning's mother filed a lawsuit against Epic Games for copyright infringement, which resulted in other developers, such as Playground Games, removing similar emotes from their titles to avoid potential litigation. In some educational settings, such as the Ilfracombe Junior School in Devon, England, the dance was banned due to perceived associations with bullying and violence. Despite these controversies, the Floss remains a recognizable cultural artifact of the late 2010s digital era.

sections.origins_and_history: The dance originated in online video culture, with the earliest known instance dating to October 2010. It was later popularized by Russell Horning in 2017 and integrated into video game culture via Fortnite.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dancer performs rapid, parallel arm swings alternating left and right with clenched fists. The movement includes counter-hip swings and a specific pattern of two swings in front of the body followed by one swing behind the body, while maintaining a stare directed straight ahead.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed as a social media trend, a video game emote, and in television performances. It has been associated with school environments and youth culture.
sections.notable_figures: Russell Horning (the 'backpack kid'), Justin Stewart, and Andrew Scites.

claims.text: The dance involves parallel arm swings, counter-hip movements, and a stare directed straight ahead.
claims.quote: Floss (englisch, deutsch Zahnseide) ist eine Tanzform, bei der beide Arme parallel abwechselnd nach links und rechts geschwungen werden, mit gegenläufigen Hüftbewegungen und geballten Fäusten. Nach zwei Schwüngen vor dem Körper wird einer mit einem Arm hinter dem Körper ausgeführt. Das ganze wird mit großer Geschwindigkeit durchgeführt. Dazu gehört ein starr geradeaus gerichteter Blick.
